html:
The Montenegrin independence referendum was held on 21 May 2006, and 55.5 percent voted to leave the union with Serbia, just above the 55 percent the European Union had required.

After the breakup of Yugoslavia, Montenegro had stayed with Serbia, first in a smaller Yugoslavia and from 2003 in a loose state union. Its leader Milo Đukanović broke with Milošević in the late 1990s and steered toward independence. The vote split the country between those who saw themselves as Montenegrins and those who saw themselves as Serbs. Independence was declared on 3 June 2006. Montenegro joined NATO in 2017 and uses the euro without being in the eurozone.
sum: The Montenegrin independence referendum was held on 21 May 2006, and 55.5 percent voted to leave the union with Serbia, just above the 55 percent the European Union had required.
